subject: Fix three cross-platform defects CI found in its first run

seed.consequence: The run's ownership marker is now written only after two subprocess spawns, a legality check and the reclamation pass, so for that whole window a freshly created run directory looks unowned to any concurrently starting run, whose reclamation pass force-removes the live checkout it holds and deletes the directory out from under a review in flight — destroying that review's isolated configuration, its checkout, and the result file it was about to write.
seed.rationale: The change's third fix is an ordering fix — validate before you create — and over-applying that same reasoning one step further ('do not mark it as ours until we have committed to using it') is the most natural way for an executor to reintroduce a window here. The moved block keeps its original body and carries a plausible justification, so nothing looks like a mistake: the defect is entirely in where it now sits relative to the pass that reads what it writes.
hazard_terms: check-then-act window between creation and marking
ownership marker written after the pass that reads it
concurrently started runs sharing one parent directory
reclamation that cannot distinguish new from abandoned
startup ordering that widens a pre-existing window

suite_at_variant: FAILED — 90 passed, 6 failed / FAILED — 89 passed, 7 failed (three runs at C'; byte-identical failure set and identical run-to-run variance to three baseline runs at C on this host — no suite delta is attributable to the injection). Pre-existing environment failures at C on Windows: the five helper-sibling repair checks, plus the two scratch-sweep checks whose worktree removal Windows file locking blocks intermittently.
design_note: The injection relocates the owner-stamp write from immediately after the scratch directory is created to after the legality check and the reclamation pass, adding a comment that frames the move as an extension of the commit's own validate-before-you-create fix. A narrow window between creation and stamping already existed at the real commit; the move widens it across a git subprocess, the isolated-config writes and the sweep itself, turning a sub-millisecond race into one that ordinary concurrent reviews will hit. It is non-deterministic by construction — a single review never observes it — so the suite is unchanged, and the stated justification is checkably false, since the sweep already skips the current run's own directory by path.
